regions.name: The Sarn Meads
regions.terrain: plain, open meadow and grass north and east of the great lake
regions.water: the Sarn and many small streams running to the lake
regions.climate: cool temperate; long winter, mild by the water
regions.notes: Held by Dunmarrow as far as the lake basin; grazing and scattered farms.

regions.name: The Hoarfells
regions.terrain: mountain, the western half of the snow range, falling to moor in the north-west
regions.water: snowmelt streams; the head of the Lorn
regions.climate: cold; snow most of the year on the tops
regions.notes: Empty high country. No people holds it. Herders in summer on the south slopes.

regions.name: Ternstrand
regions.terrain: mountain, snow-holding high ground cut by short steep valleys that run north to a cold coast
regions.water: the Tern and other short cold rivers; a small lake in the long valley
regions.climate: cold; valleys close in winter, the coast grey and windy
regions.notes: The country of the people god-ice comes to. The valleys are data finer than the paint.

regions.name: Skarness
regions.terrain: coast, cold ochre hills and headlands east of the snow range
regions.elevation: low to middling, sea level to 2,000 feet
regions.water: short streams; no great river
regions.climate: cold; long winter, sea fog
regions.notes: Open country: fishers and sealers in scattered steadings.

regions.name: The Harlfells
regions.terrain: mountain, the highest range of the land, with notched passes
regions.water: snowmelt; Dath Water; streams south-west to the lake country
regions.climate: cold; passes shut from first snow to the thaw
regions.notes: The deepest old stone in the land. Sealed doors in its roots.

regions.name: Garran Lee
regions.terrain: coast, dry ochre hills in the lee of the high range, running to the eastern sea
regions.elevation: low to middling, sea level to 2,500 feet
regions.water: few streams, dry in late summer
regions.climate: cool and dry; in the rain shadow of the range
regions.notes: Open country: goat herders, a few fishing coves.

regions.name: The Harrow Roughs
regions.terrain: hill, rough dry foothills between the high range and the great forest
regions.water: thin streams running south into the forest
regions.climate: cool and dry; hard winter
regions.notes: Open country, no rule: scattered hill steadings and charcoal burners.

regions.name: Kessmar Vale
regions.terrain: valley, one broad basin cupped in the high range, most of its floor a lake
regions.water: Lake Arrun fills the floor; Dath Water comes in from the north
regions.climate: cold; short summer, the lean season is spring
regions.notes: The country of the Dathri. Terraces on the slopes above the lake shore; two notches in the south wall.

regions.name: The Lornlands
regions.terrain: plain, flat green lowland of wide slow rivers, with low hills at its edges
regions.water: the Lorn and the Odran, wide and slow; floods in spring
regions.climate: cool temperate; wet springs, long autumns
regions.notes: Towns at the crossings. The western part is the country of the people god-law comes to; the eastern crossings are Dunmarrow.

regions.name: Dunmarrow
regions.terrain: plain, the wide grass and plough land of the old inland kingdom
regions.water: the upper Lorn; wells; a brine spring country
regions.climate: cool temperate; hard winters, dry summers
regions.notes: The heart of the kingdom of Dunmarrow, old and wearing.

regions.name: The Carn Hills
regions.terrain: hill, a long ridge of worn brown hills with woods on their northern feet
regions.water: small streams north to the Odran and south to the Carn
regions.climate: cool temperate; snow on the tops in winter
regions.notes: Open country between the kingdom and the western river: shepherds, old ways, one sealed door.

regions.name: Carnvale
regions.terrain: valley, the wide vale of the western river between low hills
regions.water: the Carn, wide water, the great lake's outflow
regions.climate: mild temperate; rain off the western sea
regions.notes: The country of the people god-trade comes to, at the ford; open steadings up and down the river.

regions.name: Heshshore
regions.terrain: plain, the meadow shore east and south-east of the great lake, between the water and the forest
regions.water: the lake; reed beds; streams from every side
regions.climate: mild for the land; the lake does not freeze
regions.notes: The shore people live here in a few villages. Quiet, thinning country.

regions.name: Heatherfell
regions.terrain: highland, brown heather upland with woods in its folds
regions.water: peat streams; the head of the Withy
regions.climate: mild and wet; wind and rain off the sea
regions.notes: Open country: summer grazing, a few steadings. The northern wall of the Withy valley.

regions.name: Withyhead
regions.terrain: valley, the upper valley of the Withy with its lake and woods
regions.water: the upper Withy; the Withymere
regions.climate: mild and wet
regions.notes: Open country: woodcutters and a few farms. The track from the ford country comes down here.

regions.name: Stonnerfell
regions.terrain: highland, heather upland and old woods south of the Withy, running to the south-west coast
regions.water: peat streams to the Withy and the sea
regions.climate: mild and wet
regions.notes: Open country. The southern wall of the Withy valley.

regions.name: Sallowdene
regions.terrain: valley, a broad river valley of water meadows, hedged fields, orchards and old woods between two heather uplands
regions.water: the Withy, marked by willows; floods on the meadows in spring
regions.climate: the mildest country of the land; late wet springs
regions.notes: The home of the Sallowfolk, who call it so. Thirteen hamlets, no town.

regions.name: Withymouth
regions.terrain: valley, the lower Withy and its reedy mouth on the south coast
regions.water: the lower Withy; salt marsh at the mouth
regions.climate: mild; sea mist
regions.notes: Open country: eel fishers, a few farms, no town.

regions.name: Ellen Heath
regions.terrain: highland, high open brown heath, treeless, with old mounds
regions.water: peat pools; few streams
regions.climate: windy and cool; snow lies in winter
regions.notes: Open country: almost no one. Old straight ways under the heather.

regions.name: Sorrel Heath
regions.terrain: highland, brown heath east of the long river
regions.water: peat pools; small streams to the Maud
regions.climate: windy and cool
regions.notes: Open country: herders from the river in summer.

regions.name: Maudvale
regions.terrain: valley, the long river's middle course, braided, with wet meadows along it
regions.water: the Maud, rising in springs under the lake's southern rim; many channels; spring floods
regions.climate: cool temperate; milder than the heath on either side
regions.notes: The country of the people god-rivers comes to. The most-worked river in the land: weirs on weirs.

regions.name: The Maudmire
regions.terrain: marsh, the dark wooded marsh of the long river's delta
regions.water: the Maud in many mouths; brackish toward the sea
regions.climate: mild and wet; fevers in summer
regions.notes: Open country: reed cutters and fowlers; no road, boat ways only.

regions.name: Hollin Ridge
regions.terrain: hill, a ridge of brown hills south of the fen
regions.water: springs on the south side that feed the Skein
regions.climate: cool; drier than the fen
regions.notes: Open country: shepherds. The dark line past the water, seen from the fen.

regions.name: Ammerholt
regions.terrain: forest, one great dark old forest
regions.water: dark streams south to the fen
regions.climate: cool and still; snow lies long under the trees
regions.notes: Open country, almost empty in its heart. Dark at noon.

regions.name: Vestfen
regions.terrain: marsh, fen and reed along the forest's southern edge, with the river sliding through it
regions.water: the Vest; meres and reed beds
regions.climate: cool, damp, misty
regions.notes: The country of the Merrowen: a walled seat on a rise at the fen's edge, steadings scattered.

regions.name: The Koldry Hills
regions.terrain: hill, steep wooded hills between the forest and the eastern sea
regions.water: short fast streams east to the sea
regions.climate: cool; sea fog
regions.notes: The country of the Oum, the one people of the land who are not human. Few, old, keeping to themselves.

regions.name: The Skeinlands
regions.terrain: plain, low misty country of many braided rivers with wooded banks and few fords
regions.water: the Skein in many threads
regions.climate: mild and misty; autumn low water
regions.notes: The round of the moving people god-secrets comes to; old landings where the water has moved away.

regions.name: The Ysk Flats
regions.terrain: coast, pale salt flats and pans along the south-east coast
regions.water: the mouths of the Skein; brine pans
regions.climate: mild and dry in summer; glare off the flats
regions.notes: The salt of the land. Held by the salt towns of Ysk.

regions.name: Orsk Shore
regions.terrain: coast, low farmed coast between the delta and the salt flats
regions.water: small rivers; wells
regions.climate: mild
regions.notes: Held by the salt towns: grain and fishing for the pans.

regions.name: Lake Hesh
regions.terrain: lake, the great still lake at the middle of the land
regions.water: deep, dark, still; it does not freeze and the wind does not move it; one outflow west, the Carn
regions.climate: mild; mist at dawn
regions.notes: Larger than any telling of it. The shore people do not fish the deep water.

regions.name: The Grey Sea
regions.terrain: sea, the cold northern sea
regions.water: salt water
regions.climate: cold; ice in the inlets in hard winters
regions.notes: No one sails it far.

regions.name: The Eastern Sea
regions.terrain: sea, the eastern sea
regions.water: salt water
regions.climate: cool; fog
regions.notes: Fishing along the coast only.

regions.name: The South Sea
regions.terrain: sea, the southern sea
regions.water: salt water
regions.climate: mild
regions.notes: Coasting boats of the salt towns.

regions.name: The Western Sea
regions.terrain: sea, the western sea, where the rain comes from
regions.water: salt water
regions.climate: mild and wet
regions.notes: Coasting only. One small island far out.

features.name: The Lorn
features.notes: Wide and slow below Averby. Rises under the Hoarfells.

features.name: The Odran
features.notes: Joins the Lorn at Tollen. Widens into Lake Odran on its upper course.

features.name: The Sarn
features.notes: Runs to the great lake.

features.name: Dath Water
features.notes: Snowmelt into Lake Arrun. The lake has no outflow anyone has found.

features.name: The Carn
features.notes: The great lake's one outflow. Wide water; fordable at Carnford in low season.

features.name: The Withy
features.known_to: the Sallowfolk; the open steadings up and down it
features.notes: Named for its willows. Floods the meadows in spring.

features.name: The Maud
features.known_to: everyone along it; the salt towns
features.notes: Rises in springs under the lake's southern rim. Braided in its middle course. The most-worked river in the land.

features.name: The Skein
features.known_to: the moving people; the salt towns
features.notes: The main thread of many. Its channels move.

features.name: The Vest
features.notes: Slides through the fen to the eastern sea.

features.name: The Tern
features.notes: A short cold river in a long valley; data finer than the paint.

features.name: Lake Arrun
features.notes: Fills most of the cupped valley's floor. The plan asked a valley; the paint gave a valley with a lake in it.

features.name: The Withymere
features.known_to: Withyhead folk; Sallowfolk who go up the track
features.notes: A lake on the upper Withy.

features.name: Lake Odran
features.notes: A made lake no one remembers making. A drowned town lies under it.

features.name: Ternlake
features.notes: A small lake below the valley head. Freezes early.

features.name: Ternaby
features.notes: The walled seat of the people god-ice comes to, near the valley mouth. Its people call it the seat or the wall.

features.name: Scour Gap
features.notes: The way south out of the long valley. Shut from first snow to the thaw.

features.name: The Scour Way
features.notes: A beaten track from the cold coast over the gap to Hallisk.

features.name: The Iceway
features.known_to: almost no one; a herder's tale
features.notes: A straight old road that shows under the ice in a low-snow year.

features.name: Kessmar
features.known_to: the Dathri; traders named to pass
features.notes: The town of the Dathri, of fitted and dry-laid stone, on the south shore of Lake Arrun.

features.name: Harl Notch
features.notes: The western notch in the valley's south wall. The widest and most used.

features.name: Venn Notch
features.notes: The eastern notch. Steeper; leads down to the Harrow Roughs.

features.name: The Harl Way
features.notes: The trade track from Kessmar over Harl Notch to Pellam. Salt and bronze come in by it.

features.name: The Venn Track
features.notes: A herders' track over Venn Notch to the forest's edge.

features.name: Gathol Door
features.known_to: the Dathri, as a place not to dig
features.notes: A sealed door in the mountain's root. Behind it the old way runs under the range for some tens of miles to Nether Door: cut gallery, side chambers, a stair, a round vault; in it a door with no handle on the near side, and one set of bones with an agreement in its hand. Underground, data only.

features.name: Nether Door
features.known_to: a few hill steadings of the Roughs
features.notes: The far end of the old way under the range. Sealed.

features.name: Rib Hollow
features.notes: A cave with great bones in it.

features.name: Tollen
features.notes: The market town at the meeting of the Lorn and the Odran, with a toll-post at the water. Its people call it the Crossing.

features.name: The Tallstones
features.notes: A line of boundary stones along the river terrace, carved with terms no one can now read.

features.name: Averby
features.notes: A crossing town of Dunmarrow on the Lorn.

features.name: Sunken Odran
features.notes: The drowned town under Lake Odran. Roofs show in a dry year.

features.name: The Turnings
features.notes: A small labyrinth of low walls above ground on the north-west coast, with its exit marked.

features.name: The Marrow Road
features.notes: The kingdom's road from Tollen by Averby and Hallisk to Pellam. Old, kept in part.

features.name: The Carn Road
features.notes: An old road from Averby over the Carn Hills to the ford. An older straight road runs under it.

features.name: The Bank Road
features.notes: The road along the Carn from the sea to the lake.

features.name: Hallisk
features.known_to: everyone in the north and west
features.notes: The old capital of Dunmarrow. A court, a hall of weights, more houses than people now.

features.name: Pellam
features.notes: Dunmarrow's eastern market, where mountain stone and wool meet salt.

features.name: Brinegarth
features.notes: Brine springs and boiling houses. The kingdom's own salt, never enough.

features.name: Dryhythe
features.notes: A stone ferry landing with no river beside it, on an old dry channel.

features.name: Carnford
features.known_to: everyone on the roads of the west
features.notes: The walled town at the ford where the Carn Road meets the Bank Road. Its people call it the Ford.

features.name: Carn Vault
features.known_to: no one living; drovers know the hollow sound
features.notes: A vault under the old road where the Carn Road crosses the hills.

features.name: Wether Door
features.notes: A sealed door in a hillside.

features.name: Carnmouth
features.notes: A fishing and landing village at the river's mouth.

features.name: The Fell Way
features.known_to: Carnford drovers; Withyhead folk; the Sallowfolk
features.notes: A beaten track from the ford over Heatherfell and down the upper Withy.

features.name: The Foot Track
features.notes: The worn cart track along the foot of the northern slope of Sallowdene and on down the valley. Under part of it runs one of the old straight roads.

features.name: Merestead
features.notes: A few farms below the Withymere.

features.name: Eelstow
features.notes: Eel fishers at the river's mouth.

features.name: Sallowford
features.notes: The river crossing where the reeves meet, with a market ground that fills a few days a year. The Sallowfolk call it the crossing.

features.name: Kettling Hall
features.notes: A roofless stone hall by the old track, at the edge of the highest hamlet. Older than the Sallowfolk. They call it the old hall.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 1
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 2
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 3
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 4
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 5
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 6
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 7
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 8
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 9
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 10
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 11
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 12
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play.

features.name: unnamed hamlet 13
features.notes: A hamlet of Sallowdene; its name is left for play. The highest hamlet, where the upland starts.

features.name: The Comb Barrows
features.known_to: a few heath herders, who keep away
features.notes: A huge and ancient abandoned apiary on the high heath: rows of stone-built hive houses under turf, with wax in them older than the kingdoms.

features.name: The Posted Door
features.notes: A door in a hillside, shut on purpose, with a carved notice beside it that no one reads.

features.name: Maudry
features.notes: The walled town at the bend in the middle reach. Its people call themselves the people of the Bend.

features.name: The Weir Path
features.notes: The towpath and track along the Maud.

features.name: Nenna
features.notes: A village of the north shore.

features.name: Lowater
features.notes: A village of the east shore.

features.name: Ammot
features.notes: The village where the Carn leaves the lake.

features.name: unnamed fallen stone
features.notes: A warm blue-grey stone, heavy for its size, that fell in the forest the night the gods came down. 63 hundredths of the way from Kessmar to Vesthallow (r-0140, r-0141).

features.name: Farholm
features.known_to: a story on the west coast
features.notes: A small island far out in the western sea, past a long crossing. Finer than the paint.

features.name: Vesthallow
features.notes: The walled seat of the Merrowen on a rise at the fen's edge.

features.name: Grayle Ford
features.notes: A gravel ford on the Skein, one of the few.

features.name: Lowhythe
features.known_to: the moving people; the salt towns
features.notes: The winter seat of the moving people on a sheltered bend: timber and turf houses, empty half the year.

features.name: Hollin Spring
features.notes: The spring at the head of the Skein.

features.name: Dry Stairs
features.notes: An old stone landing where the water has moved away.

features.name: Yskar
features.notes: The chief of the salt towns, on the flats.

features.name: Orsk
features.notes: A salt town and grain port west of the flats.

features.name: Varn
features.notes: A salt town at the mouths of the Skein.

features.name: Lowgrave Field
features.notes: An old burial ground whose graves are dug far too deep for their dead.

features.name: The Salt Way
features.notes: The carriers' track from the salt towns over Hollin Ridge to the fen.

features.name: Koldry
features.notes: The hold of the Oum.

features.name: Ammeth Hall
features.notes: A hall of forgotten purpose in the hills, with a stair under a sealed door.

features.name: Skarhaven
features.notes: A sealers' and fishers' haven.
